data.name: Eknaath
data.gender_notes: Eknaath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Eknaath is derived from Sanskrit words 'Ek' meaning one and 'Nath' meaning lord. This name signifies being devoted to one supreme deity or being the one who leads others towards the path of God. The name Eknaath carries the meaning “One Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Eknaath usually hope their child will grow to embody one lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Eknaath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eknaath total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eknaath has historical significance in the Hindu culture, as it reflects the concept of monotheism prevalent in Hinduism. The moniker 'Ek' is a testimonial to the belief in the existence of one supreme deity, which is a core tenet in Hinduism. Additionally, the name indicates a strong, unwavering devotion to this one God, a sentiment greatly valued during ancient times when religious affiliations played a crucial role in societal structures. Further, the name Eknaath may also denote the one who leads others towards the path of God, symbolizing a spiritual leader.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, Eknaath is a moniker reminiscent of the deep devotion and unwavering faith that one should have in the divine. This name furthers the notion of unity with the Supreme Being, reaffirming the age-old concept of 'Ekam Sat Vipra Bahudha Vadanti,' which signifies 'The Truth is One, but the Sages Call It by Various Names.' The name Eknaath, therefore, serves as a constant reminder of the importance of having a strong spiritual bond with the divine and is an embodiment of the spiritual practice of devotion and steadfastness towards the Almighty.

historical_references.reference: Eknaath was a prominent Maratha warrior and a key figure in the consolidation of the Maratha Empire under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. He played a crucial role in the Battle of Pratapgarh (1659), which is considered as the founding day of the Maratha Empire.
historical_references.context: Maratha Empire, Battle of Pratapgarh, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj

historical_references.reference: Eknaath was also known as 'Netaji' (General) in the Maratha army and was a close advisor and commander to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. He led several military campaigns and fortifications, including the construction of the Rajgad Fort.
historical_references.context: Maratha army, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Military campaigns, Fortifications
